title: Reading strategies
goal: Read TEF and TCF Canada documents efficiently: skim for the purpose, scan for details, spot paraphrase traps and manage your 60 minutes.

blocks.title: After a practice reading test in Ottawa
blocks.context: Raj is preparing for the TEF Canada. He talks to Lucie, his tutor at a community centre.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Alors, Raj, ce premier test de lecture, ça s'est passé comment ?
lines.en: So, Raj, how did this first reading test go?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Pas très bien. Je lisais chaque document du début à la fin, et à la question 25, il ne me restait plus que dix minutes.
lines.en: Not very well. I was reading every document from beginning to end, and at question 25, I only had ten minutes left.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: C'est l'erreur classique. Au TEF, tu as une heure pour quarante questions : ça fait à peu près une minute et demie par question.
lines.en: That's the classic mistake. In the TEF, you have one hour for forty questions: that's about a minute and a half per question.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: En plus, j'ai laissé huit questions vides, parce que je n'étais pas sûr.
lines.en: And I left eight questions blank, because I wasn't sure.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Ça, il ne faut jamais le faire ! Une mauvaise réponse ne te fait pas perdre de points. Une réponse vide, par contre, c'est zéro à coup sûr.
lines.en: You must never do that! A wrong answer doesn't make you lose points. A blank answer, on the other hand, is a guaranteed zero.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: D'accord. Et pour aller plus vite, je fais comment ?
lines.en: OK. And how do I go faster?

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Tu lis d'abord la question. Ensuite, tu regardes quel type de document c'est, et tu cherches seulement l'information dont tu as besoin.
lines.en: First you read the question. Then you look at what type of document it is, and you look only for the information you need.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Mais souvent, je retrouve les mots de l'option dans le texte, et pourtant ma réponse est fausse !
lines.en: But I often find the words of the option in the text, and yet my answer is wrong!

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: C'est normal : la bonne réponse reformule le texte avec d'autres mots. Quand une option recopie le texte mot pour mot, méfie-toi !
lines.en: That's normal: the right answer rephrases the text in other words. When an option copies the text word for word, be suspicious!

blocks.body: New expressions: [[à coup sûr]] = for sure, guaranteed; [[mot pour mot]] = word for word; [[se méfier]] = to be wary, not to trust. Lucie uses [[tu]] because Raj and she have worked together for months.

steps.title: How to read in an exam

blocks.title: Two reading tests, two rhythms
blocks.body:
Both exams give you **60 minutes** of multiple-choice reading, but they are not organised the same way. Know your exam before you train, because the timing strategy changes.

In both, **every answer is in the document**. You never need outside knowledge, and you never need to understand every word.

blocks.title: Reading at a glance
head: TEF Canada
TCF Canada
rows: Multiple choice, 1 point each, **no penalty** for a wrong answer
Multiple choice on documents of **increasing difficulty**
About 90 seconds on average: faster at the start, slower at the end
Answer **every** question. Stuck? Mark it, guess, move on.
Bank the easy points quickly and **keep time for the long texts** at the end.
blocks.note: For both exams, a blank answer can never earn a point. Never leave a question empty when the time is almost over.

blocks.title: The six-step routine for each question
blocks.pattern: question → type de document → repérer → vérifier la reformulation → éliminer → répondre
blocks.note:
1. **Read the question first** (and the options), so you know what you are looking for.
2. **Identify the document**: an ad, an email, an article? Its type tells you where the answer usually is.
3. **Scan** for the zone that answers the question.
4. Read those two or three sentences **in detail**, and check which option **says the same thing in other words**.
5. **Eliminate** the options that are false, too strong, or true but off-topic.
6. **Answer** and move on.

examples.en: What is the purpose of this email?
Who is this ad aimed at?

examples.fr: Selon l'article, pourquoi la ville a-t-elle changé l'horaire ?
examples.en: According to the article, why did the city change the schedule?

examples.fr: Que doivent faire les locataires avant le 15 mai ?
examples.en: What must the tenants do before May 15?

blocks.title: Skim or scan?
blocks.body:
**Skim** ([[lecture globale]]): 15 to 20 seconds on the title, the first sentence, the layout and the signature. You find the **type**, the **purpose** and the **audience**. Use it for questions like [[Quel est le but de ce document ?]] or [[À qui s'adresse ce texte ?]].

**Scan** ([[lecture sélective]]): you hunt for one thing, such as a date, a price, a name or a condition. Your eyes jump over the text; you slow down only around the target.

**Read in detail** only the zone that contains the answer. That is where paraphrase traps live, so read every small word there: [[sauf]], [[seulement]], [[ne… que]], [[au plus tard]], [[dès]], [[sans]].

blocks.title: Document types: where the answer usually is
head: Document
Look first at…
Typical question
rows: the title, the price, the conditions in small print
the subject line (Objet), the first and last paragraphs
the title, the lead paragraph, the first sentence of each paragraph
headings, dates, what is forbidden or required
rows, columns and the notes marked with *
À quelle heure part le dernier autobus ?
each person's first and last sentences: that is where the opinion is

blocks.title: The four paraphrase traps
blocks.body:
Imagine the text says: [[La piscine sera fermée du 3 au 10 juillet pour des travaux.]]

- **The word-match trap.** The option reuses the words of the text but changes the meaning: [[La piscine ouvrira le 3 juillet après les travaux.]] Same words, wrong fact. The correct option sounds different: [[On ne pourra pas nager à la piscine pendant une semaine, début juillet.]]
- **True, but not the answer.** The option is correct according to the text, but it answers another question. If the question asks *why* the pool is closed, [[La piscine est fermée une semaine]] is true but useless.
- **Too strong.** The text says [[parfois]] or [[la plupart des]]; the option says [[toujours]] or [[tous]]. One word makes it false.
- **The small word that flips everything.** [[sauf]] (except), [[ne… que]] (only), [[au plus tard]] (at the latest), [[dès]] (from… on), [[sans]] (without). Read them twice.

blocks.title: Paraphrases you will meet again and again
blocks.body: Learn these pairs. In the exam, the text uses one side and the right option uses the other.

examples.fr: gratuit = sans frais = vous n'aurez rien à payer
Il est interdit de fumer. = On n'a pas le droit de fumer.
à partir du 1er mars = dès le 1er mars
Les inscriptions sont closes. = Il n'est plus possible de s'inscrire.
Le spectacle est reporté. = Le spectacle aura lieu plus tard.
en raison du mauvais temps = à cause de la météo

blocks.title: Why you should answer everything
blocks.body:
With four options, a pure guess is right **one time in four**. If Raj guesses his eight blank questions, he should win about **2 points** instead of 0. If he can first eliminate two options, his chances rise to **one in two**: about 4 points.

On the TEF, there is no penalty for a wrong answer, so guessing costs nothing. On both exams, a blank is always zero. Keep the last **two minutes** to fill in every empty answer.

blocks.title: Canadian documents
blocks.body:
TEF and TCF Canada documents often come from everyday life in Canada. Expect Québec and Canadian words such as [[courriel]] (email), [[stationnement]] (parking), [[fin de semaine]] (weekend), [[dépanneur]] (convenience store), [[aréna]] (skating rink), [[CLSC]] (a local health and social services centre in Québec) and housing ads with [[3 ½]] or [[4 ½]].

Prices are written with the dollar sign **after** the number and a comma for cents: [[12,50 $]]. Dates have no capital letter: [[le lundi 3 juin]].

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: These are the question types you will read most often. Say them aloud so you recognise them instantly.

lines.fr: Quel est le but de ce document ?
lines.en: What is the purpose of this document?
Who is this message aimed at?

lines.fr: Selon l'auteur, pourquoi le projet a-t-il été abandonné ?
lines.en: According to the author, why was the project abandoned?
lines.tip: a-t-il: the t is added for the sound, and you pronounce it.

lines.fr: Que doit faire le lecteur avant le 30 avril ?
lines.en: What must the reader do before April 30?

lines.fr: Il s'agit d'une annonce de location.

blocks.fr: Selon le courriel, les inscriptions sont closes.
blocks.explain: [[closes]] is the feminine plural of [[clos]] (closed), agreeing with [[les inscriptions]].

blocks.fr: Ouvert tous les jours, sauf le lundi.
blocks.explain: [[sauf]] = except. One small word, and the answer changes.

steps.title: Practice: two documents
steps.intro: Time yourself: about **90 seconds per question**, as in the exam. Read the question first, then go to the document.

blocks.title: Document 1: A notice at the library
blocks.fr:
BIBLIOTHÈQUE DU PLATEAU — AVIS AUX USAGERS
En raison de travaux de rénovation, la bibliothèque sera fermée du 3 au 16 juin. Pendant cette période, vous pourrez rapporter vos livres dans la boîte de retour extérieure, sauf les DVD, qui doivent être rendus au comptoir de la bibliothèque du Mile-End.
Il n'y aura pas de frais de retard pendant la fermeture.
Réouverture le lundi 17 juin, avec un nouvel espace pour les enfants !
blocks.en: PLATEAU LIBRARY — NOTICE TO USERS. Because of renovation work, the library will be closed from June 3 to 16. During this period, you can return your books in the outdoor return box, except DVDs, which must be returned to the counter of the Mile-End library. There will be no late fees during the closure. Reopening on Monday, June 17, with a new space for children!

blocks.prompt: What is the main purpose of this notice?
options: Informer les usagers d'une fermeture temporaire.
Présenter le nouvel espace pour les enfants.
Annoncer que la bibliothèque déménage au Mile-End.
Demander aux usagers de rendre leurs livres avant le 3 juin.
blocks.explain: Skim the title and the first sentence: [[sera fermée du 3 au 16 juin]]. The notice exists to tell users about a temporary closure.
optionFeedback: True, but it is only a detail at the end: *true but not the answer*.
Word-match trap: Mile-End is only where you return DVDs. Nothing says the library is moving.
Nothing asks you to return books before June 3; you can use the outdoor box during the closure.

blocks.prompt: You borrowed a DVD and want to return it on June 10. What must you do?
options: Le rapporter dans une autre bibliothèque.
Le mettre dans la boîte de retour extérieure.
Attendre la réouverture et payer des frais de retard.
Le déposer au comptoir du Plateau.
blocks.explain: [[sauf les DVD, qui doivent être rendus au comptoir de la bibliothèque du Mile-End]]: the right option paraphrases this as “another library”.
optionFeedback: The small word [[sauf]] excludes DVDs from the outdoor box.
There are no late fees during the closure, and you don't have to wait.
The Plateau library is closed on June 10.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence means the same as « Il n'y aura pas de frais de retard pendant la fermeture » ?
options: Si vous rendez un livre en retard pendant les travaux, vous ne paierez rien.
Pendant la fermeture, les frais de retard seront moins chers.
Il n'y aura pas de retard dans les travaux.
Les livres en retard doivent être rendus avant la fermeture.
blocks.explain: [[pas de frais]] = nothing to pay. Option 3 is a word-match trap: it reuses [[retard]] with a completely different meaning (a delay in the work).

blocks.title: Document 2: An email
blocks.fr:
Objet : Votre inscription – atelier « Réussir son entrevue »

Bonjour Madame Benali,

Nous avons bien reçu votre inscription à l'atelier du jeudi 12 septembre. Malheureusement, la formatrice est malade, et l'atelier est reporté au jeudi 19 septembre, à la même heure.
Si cette nouvelle date ne vous convient pas, merci de nous répondre au plus tard le 16 septembre : nous vous proposerons une place dans le groupe d'octobre.

Cordialement,
Karim Haddad
Service d'aide à l'emploi
blocks.en: Subject: Your registration – “Succeed in your interview” workshop. Hello Ms. Benali, We have received your registration for the workshop on Thursday, September 12. Unfortunately, the trainer is ill, and the workshop is postponed to Thursday, September 19, at the same time. If this new date doesn't suit you, please reply by September 16 at the latest: we will offer you a place in the October group. Best regards, Karim Haddad, Employment Help Service

options: Pour signaler un changement de date.
Pour annuler l'atelier définitivement.
Pour confirmer que l'atelier a lieu le 12 septembre.
Pour inscrire Mme Benali dans le groupe d'octobre.
blocks.explain: [[reporté au jeudi 19 septembre]] = moved to a later date. A postponement is a change of date, not a cancellation.
optionFeedback: Too strong: [[reporté]] means postponed, not cancelled.
That was the original date; it is no longer valid.
October is only an option *if* the new date doesn't suit her.

blocks.prompt: Ms. Benali is not free on September 19. What should she do?
options: Prévenir le service d'ici le 16 septembre.
Venir le 12 septembre comme prévu.
Appeler directement la formatrice.
Attendre le mois d'octobre sans répondre.
blocks.explain: [[merci de nous répondre au plus tard le 16 septembre]] is paraphrased as [[prévenir le service d'ici le 16 septembre]] ([[d'ici le]] = by).

blocks.prompt: Match each expression from the documents with its paraphrase.
pairs: déplacé à une date plus tardive

blocks.text: Ce courriel ___ aux personnes inscrites à l'atelier.
blocks.en: This email is aimed at the people registered for the workshop.
blocks.explain: [[s'adresser à]] = to be aimed at. [[Il s'agit de]] only works with the impersonal [[il]]: [[il s'agit d'un courriel]].

blocks.text: Dans le document 1, il ___ d'un avis de fermeture.
blocks.explain: [[Il s'agit de]] + noun = it is (about)… The subject is always [[il]]: never [[le document s'agit]].

blocks.prompt: According to the email, the workshop has been postponed.
accept: Selon le courriel, l'atelier a été reporté.
D'après le courriel, l'atelier a été reporté.
Selon le courriel, l'atelier est reporté.
D'après le courriel, l'atelier est reporté.
L'atelier a été reporté, selon le courriel.
L'atelier a été reporté, d'après le courriel.
L'atelier est reporté, selon le courriel.
L'atelier est reporté, d'après le courriel.
blocks.explain: [[Selon]] or [[d'après]] = according to. [[a été reporté]] is the passive in the passé composé, as in news texts.

blocks.prompt: TEF reading: 3 minutes left and 6 questions unanswered. What is the best move?
options: Answer all six, eliminating what you can, even if you have to guess.
Answer the two you are surest of and leave the rest blank.
Use the time to recheck your earlier answers.
blocks.explain: There is no penalty for a wrong answer on the TEF, and a blank is always zero. Fill in everything first; recheck only if time remains.

blocks.title: An ad from a sports centre
blocks.fr:
CENTRE SPORTIF SAINT-LAURENT
Cours de natation pour adultes débutants, le mardi de 19 h à 20 h.
Gratuit pour les résidents de Saint-Laurent, 60 $ pour les autres.
Inscription obligatoire en ligne avant le 30 avril.
Bonnet de bain exigé.
blocks.en: SAINT-LAURENT SPORTS CENTRE. Swimming lessons for adult beginners, on Tuesdays from 7 to 8 p.m. Free for Saint-Laurent residents, $60 for others. Online registration required before April 30. Swimming cap required.

blocks.prompt: Write an exam question about this ad in French, then three options: one correct option that paraphrases the ad, and two traps (for example, a word-match trap and a “too strong” option). Mark the correct one and add a short note on why each trap is wrong.
blocks.promptFr: Écrivez une question d'examen sur cette annonce, avec une bonne réponse et deux pièges.
checklist: A real question that the ad answers (Qui… ? Que… ? Quand… ?)
A correct option that does NOT copy the ad word for word
A word-match trap that reuses words from the ad
A “too strong” or “true but not the answer” trap
A short note explaining each trap

models.label: Model answer
models.fr:
Question : Qui peut suivre ce cours sans payer ?
A. Les adultes qui habitent à Saint-Laurent. C'est la bonne réponse.
B. Tous les adultes débutants. Trop fort : c'est seulement pour les résidents.
C. Les personnes inscrites avant le 30 avril. Mots du texte, mais l'inscription n'est pas la condition pour la gratuité.
models.en: Question: Who can take this course without paying? A. Adults who live in Saint-Laurent. That's the right answer. B. All adult beginners. Too strong: it's only for residents. C. People registered before April 30. Words from the text, but registration isn't the condition for it being free.

models.label: Stronger model answer
models.fr:
Question : Que doit faire une personne qui n'habite pas à Saint-Laurent et qui veut suivre ce cours ?
A. S'inscrire sur Internet d'ici la fin avril et payer 60 $. Bonne réponse : elle reformule l'annonce.
B. Venir le mardi à 19 h avec son bonnet de bain, sans inscription. Piège : l'inscription est obligatoire.
C. Habiter à Saint-Laurent avant le 30 avril. Piège : on reprend des mots du texte, mais le sens est complètement différent.
models.en: Question: What must a person who doesn't live in Saint-Laurent and wants to take this course do? A. Register online by the end of April and pay $60. Right answer: it rephrases the ad. B. Come on Tuesday at 7 p.m. with a swimming cap, without registering. Trap: registration is required. C. Live in Saint-Laurent before April 30. Trap: it reuses words from the text, but the meaning is completely different.

summary:
- Know the reading format of each exam: **TEF** 40 questions in 60 min, no penalty, so answer everything; **TCF** 39 questions of increasing difficulty, so keep time for the end
- Skim for the purpose and audience, scan for details, read in detail only the answer zone
- Spot the four traps: word-match, true but off-topic, too strong, and small words like [[sauf]], [[ne… que]], [[au plus tard]]
- Understand question stems: [[Quel est le but de… ?]], [[À qui s'adresse… ?]], [[Selon l'article…]]
